correctness.rationale: Exact conditional Gaussian variance is 2DτF(u) with F(u)=u−3/2+2e^−u−e^−2u/2. The Poisson-age Laplace principle has a unique saddle z=2F/(1−e^−u) by positive derivative of its parameterization; tail truncation controls u→0,∞. The drift is O(1), giving only √R perturbations. The maximal projected drift is attained to arbitrary precision with positive R-independent angular Brownian tube probability for every fixed D_r>0, while D_r=0 is deterministic. Envelope derivative gives strict J concavity and 0<J−z<3/2.

originality.rationale: Franke–Sokolov give the passive saddle and fixed-reset-rate tail. This result is restricted to the simultaneous high-reset, x∝√R rare displacement, age concentration, and a genuinely new √R active heading correction with a discontinuity at D_r=0.
